back: Medium Access Control (MAC) is a set of protocols that determine how devices on a shared network take turns using the same communication channel.

front: What does Medium Access Control Prevent?
back: Packet collisions on a shared communication medium.

front: What are the three types of controlled access protocols? (Common medium)
How does reservation based access control work?
back: Time is divided into slots, devices reserve a slot in advance and can only transmit during their reserved slot.

front: How does polling work? In access control.
back: A primary device controls all communication, polling each device in turn to ask if it has data to send. Devices can only transmit when authorised by the primary.
A unique token is passed around the network, only the device holding the token can transmit. When finished it passes the token to the next device.

front: What are the two failure risks of token passing?
back: The token can be lost if a device crashes, or duplicated causing multiple devices to transmit simultaneously.

front: What is the main weakness of all controlled access protocols?
back: They can be slow due to bottlenecks — devices may have to wait a long time before getting their turn.

front: How does CSMA/CD detect a collision?
back: While transmitting, if the voltage read back on the wire differs from what was sent, a collision has occurred.
